hero.lead: A nation of 1.26 million that reached the 95-95-95 HIV treatment targets a decade early, and where more than half of citizens still live below the poverty line.

capital.heading: 13 instruments. Water, power, roads, schools and clinics, broadband, and budget support for private-sector growth.

record.text: Water Supply and Sanitation Access Project: Rural water and sanitation, with $8m additional financing, June 2025
Network Reinforcement and Access Project: Grid and new connections
Strengthening Early Childhood Development and Basic Education Systems: Early years and basic schooling
Health System Strengthening for Human Capital Development: Health system
Public debt, share of GDP, end of fiscal year 2025/26, up from 40% a year earlier

register.name: Digital Eswatini Project
register.detail: Approved 15 June 2026 · Three World Bank commitments of $19.3M, $26M and $19.7M
register.text: A World Bank project to widen access to affordable broadband and to help the government deliver public services online. Digital access supports livelihood and the reach of education and health services.

register.name: Fiscal Management and Competitiveness Development Policy Financing, OPEC Fund co-financing
register.detail: Approved 29 July 2025 · Signed 16 January 2026 · Policy-based loan · Total programme $200M with the IBRD and the AfDB
register.note: Co-finances the World Bank reform loan
register.text: The OPEC Fund’s policy-based loan to the reform programme of the same name, co-financed with the IBRD and the African Development Bank and executed by the Ministry of Finance. The World Bank’s part of the programme is the $100 million development policy loan listed here.

register.name: Fiscal Management and Competitiveness Development Policy Loan
register.detail: Board approval announced 30 April 2025 · Development policy loan · First of a programmatic series of two
register.note: Public debt, private sector and energy reforms
register.text: Budget support for reforms to public debt management and spending arrears, the business climate and digital payments, and the opening of the electricity market to private renewable power. It builds on the 2021 to 2022 series and aims to mobilise private capital and expand energy access.

register.name: Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation (ASCENT) Eswatini
register.detail: Announced 13 February 2025 · $39M IDA, $51M IBRD, $10M Livable Planet Fund grant
register.text: Grid and off-grid electricity for 200,000 people, with 50,000 new household connections over five years, building on the Network Reinforcement and Access Project. It aims at the remaining 12% of citizens without electricity, the energy standard.

register.name: Mkhondvo-Ngwavuma Water Augmentation Program, Phase 2
register.detail: Approved 21 June 2023 · Signed 23 December 2024 · Project loan · Total cost $213.5M
register.note: Dams and irrigation in the south
register.text: The OPEC Fund’s loan to the second phase of the water augmentation programme, executed by ESWADE, with the Government, BADEA, the DBSA and the African Development Bank. Stored water for irrigated farming supports the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Strengthening Early Childhood Development and Basic Education Systems
register.text: Supports early childhood development and basic education.

register.name: Health System Strengthening for Human Capital Development
register.text: Strengthens primary care and the health system.

register.name: Water Supply and Sanitation Access Project
register.detail: Approved 10 October 2019 · Additional financing of $8M, 12 June 2025 · Investment project financing
register.text: Extends safe water and sanitation to underserved communities. The World Bank raised its financing from $45 million to $53 million in June 2025: the water standard sets Coverage in Eswatini.

register.name: Network Reinforcement and Access Project
register.text: Strengthens the grid and connects new households.

register.name: Enhancing Economic Resilience and Competitiveness Program, Phase I
register.detail: Announced July 2025 · Loan · First phase of a two-year programme
register.text: African Development Bank budget support for fiscal and public financial management reforms and for private-sector-led, inclusive and green growth. It aims to reduce domestic arrears, raise private-sector growth and increase the renewable share of energy, alongside World Bank financing.

register.name: Road links in Lubombo and Shiselweni, first stage
register.detail: Announced 9 December 2024 · Loan · 105.9 km of paved roads on the MR14 and MR21
register.note: Climate-resilient roads in the east and south
register.text: Upgrades 105.9 km of paved road on the MR14 (Siphofaneni to Nsoko) and the MR21 (Maloma to Siphambanweni), with bridges and an axle-load weighing station. It includes vocational training and apprenticeships for at least 200 young people in the Lubombo and Shiselweni regions.

register.name: New Eco-Green City Masterplan, Shiselweni
register.detail: Approved 8 June 2023 · Grant from the Urban and Municipal Development Fund
register.note: Planning a new town for an agro-processing zone
register.text: An African Development Bank grant to ESWADE for the vision, master plan and pre-feasibility studies of a new urban area in Shiselweni, linked to the Mkhondvo-Ngwavuma water programme and a planned agro-processing zone. It plans for housing, health and education services for the workers and families the zone would bring.

register.name: Lower Maguduza Hydropower Project, 13.5 MW
register.detail: Financial close announced 3 February 2025 · Standard Bank mandated lead arranger
register.note: Private hydropower for the national grid
register.text: Debt financing for a 13.5 MW hydropower plant developed by African Clean Energy Developments, whose shareholders are the IDEAS Fund managed by AIIM and the Eswatini Public Service Pensions Fund. It adds a private renewable source of power, the energy standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Health System
items.label: HIV targets met, a decade early
items.text: 94% know their status, 97% of them are on treatment, 96% of those are virally suppressed.

items.name: The Clean Power
items.label: Renewable share of electricity output, 2021
items.text: And 89.3% of citizens connected, among the highest in the region.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Sugar cane and farms across most of the country, while half of citizens are poor.
items.alt: Sugar cane fields in the Lowveld

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest, 2024
items.text: Woodland and plantations across a quarter of the kingdom.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: Three in four live in the countryside.

items.name: The Luke Commission
items.text: Mobile and pop-up clinics that take care to rural communities, where three in four citizens live; its Matsapha Mobile Clinic for factory workers sees an average of 300 people a day.

items.name: Gone Rural
items.text: A social enterprise whose model lets rural women earn an income by weaving from their homes, using Eswatini’s ancestral weaving techniques.
